title: Simple current mirror
description: A K:1 current mirror sized as unit devices: the diode-connected reference binds electrically (its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$, so the bind declares the connection and the table is read along that diagonal), and the output device binds width-first at K times the reference width, evaluated at the served output node's $V_{DS}$. The systematic error is the $\lambda$ mismatch between the two operating points; the random error is the Pelgrom spread of the ratio.

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves

params.name: L
params.note: longer L: lower lambda (systematic) error and more matching area

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: mirror inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens current matching but costs compliance headroom

params.name: err_target
params.note: systematic (lambda) error budget; cascode the mirror if this cannot close

doc.title: Reference (diode) device
doc.description: The diode-connected reference: binds at the input current, with vds tied to its own vgs by the connection rather than by an estimate. Exposes its width so the output side can size as a unit-device multiple.

rows.name: sys_err
rows.note: lambda mismatch between the output vds and the diode point

rows.name: sigma_ratio
rows.note: random 1-sigma error of the K:1 ratio; the K-times-larger output device contributes 1/sqrt(K) of the reference spread

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: output resistance the mirror presents: the output device's own r_o and nothing more. That is the whole cost of the simple mirror — the output current tracks the node voltage through gds, which is what the systematic-error row measures at one particular V_out. This is the number a stage loading the mirror sees

rules.note: output device saturated at the served node
